title: Systems & Serving track
summary: Four capstones covering the infrastructure half of ML: serve a model under load, run a real distributed training experiment, optimize inference with KV-cache + quantization, and build a production search engine. The ramp B2B teams use to qualify ML-systems hires.
contentIntro:
## What this track proves

Four capstones, in order:

1. **Build a serving stack** — you can stand up a model behind an API under load
2. **Distributed training experiment** — you can run and reason about multi-device training
3. **Inference optimization: KV-cache + quantization** — you can make serving fast and cheap, with measurements
4. **Build a production search engine** — you can ship a retrieval system end-to-end

Each produces an independently-signed public artifact; completing the required set mints a track-level credential.
contentUndergrad:
## What this track proves

The Systems & Serving track bundles four capstones into one ~20-week program covering the production-engineering half of ML — the part that determines whether a model is actually useful in production.

### The capstones (in order)

1. **[Build a serving stack](/capstones/build-a-serving-stack)** — a model behind an API with batching, health checks, and a load test.
2. **[Distributed training experiment](/capstones/distributed-training-experiment)** — a controlled multi-device training run with a scaling readout.
3. **[Inference optimization: KV-cache + quantization](/capstones/inference-optimization-kvcache-quant)** — baseline → KV-cache → INT8 → both, with a tokens/sec + memory + quality table.
4. **[Build a production search engine](/capstones/build-a-production-search-engine)** — an end-to-end retrieval system with an eval harness.

Each artifact carries a signed transcript verifiable against the published ed25519 key. Self-paced; AI tutoring + peer review run alongside.
contentGrad:
## What this track proves (for someone reading the artifact)

A learner who completes this track has demonstrated serving judgment (an API under real load with batching + observability), distributed-training literacy (a controlled multi-device run they can reason about, not just launch), inference-systems craft (an explicit production recommendation backed by their own tokens/sec + memory + quality measurements), and retrieval-systems competence (a search engine with an evaluation harness, not a demo). The defense thread covers each capstone's tradeoffs and why the four together evidence ML-systems production readiness — and where the holes are.
